metadata.title: Secure Network Platform SSPP
metadata.remarks: This System Security Plan and Profile (SSPP) template defines the security and privacy posture for the institutional Secure Network platform, which provides governed, identity-aware, policy-driven, and resilient network connectivity across all environments and access scenarios. The SSPP is structured to align with the NIST SP 800-18 SSP format and includes references to relevant NIST guidance on Zero Trust Architecture, Zero Trust Networking, and Cyber Resiliency. This template serves as a foundational reference for implementing a secure network platform that supports institutional security objectives while enabling secure and seamless connectivity for users, applications, and services.

import-profile.remarks: Institutional security, privacy, resiliency, and operational baseline.

system-characteristics.system-description: Institutional Secure Network platform providing governed, identity-aware, policy-driven, and resilient network connectivity across all environments and access scenarios.

props.name: platform-role
props.remarks: Secure Network is a Tier-0 institutional dependency; compromise or outage has cascading impact across identity, applications, and communications.

props.name: depends-on-sspp
props.remarks: Secure Network relies on Secure Identity Providers for identity assertions and authentication context.

props.name: depends-on-sspp
props.remarks: Secure Network consumes identity assurance signals to inform network access and enforcement decisions.

props.name: implements-pattern
props.remarks: This SSPP is the authoritative implementation and assurance anchor for the Secure Network composite pattern.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Secure Network enforces Zero Trust Architecture principles by eliminating implicit trust and relying on identity-, context-, and policy-based decisions.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Secure Network aligns with Zero Trust Networking guidance, supporting identity-aware, policy-mediated ingress, lateral, and egress control.

props.name: nist-guidance
props.remarks: Secure Network resiliency is designed to anticipate, withstand, recover from, and adapt to adverse conditions, preventing cascading institutional failures.

props.name: network-crypto-trust
props.remarks: All TLS, mutual TLS, VPN, and internal service authentication must rely on certificates issued and validated by the PKI Platform.

props.name: network-key-management
props.remarks: Private keys used for network services must be generated, stored, and protected within HSMs or TPMs governed by the Key Management Platform.

system-implementation.remarks: Secure Network is implemented as a composition of governed network capabilities including core transport, access control, segmentation, policy mediation, monitoring and response, egress discipline, remote and third-party access, and network resiliency.

roles.title: Network Architecture Authority
roles.remarks: Accountable for Secure Network architecture integrity, pattern alignment, and assurance.

roles.title: Network Operations
roles.remarks: Operates and maintains Secure Network services in accordance with platform governance.

roles.title: Network Security Monitoring
roles.remarks: Monitors Secure Network telemetry, detects threats, and coordinates response.

control-implementation.remarks: All network security and privacy controls are implemented by subordinate Secure Network patterns and inherited SSPPs. This SSPP serves as the authoritative governance and assurance anchor. Network services must not accept unvalidated certificates, disable certificate verification, or use embedded or application-generated private keys.
